content:
alicia: quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC — propose we adopt namespace-based shard ownership for safetensors bundles. idea: each namespace owns a contiguous shard range and a manifest that lists active variants. avoids global registry churn.
raja: curious — how do we handle warmup for cross-namespace models? e.g., shared embedding weights referenced by multiple namespaces
morgan: we split ownership vs. adoption. owner namespace publishes canonical shards. consumers can adopt a read-only overlay with a local manifest that points to owner shards. warmup picks from local overlay first, falls back to owner endpoints.
jen: that seems fine, but what's the strategy for prefix caching and eviction? we already saw OOM spikes when many adopters hotstart same embedding.
alicia: good point. proposal: add an adoption QoS tag on manifests: {"adopt_priority": "low|normal|high", "prefetch_budget": n}. adopters honor that: low => on-demand only, high => prefetch hot ranges.
raja: can we make adopters rate-limit prefetch to owner region to avoid thundering herd? maybe token-bucket per-owner with leaky-bucket backpressure.
morgan: yes, suggested implementation: owner exposes a simple HTTP endpoint /warmup-credit that awards credits per-second. adopters call it during backfill. lightweight and infra-friendly. taylor: what about consistency? if owner rotates shard variants (e.g., quantized vs fp16), adopters need a safe handoff. proposal: two-phase manifest commit: publish new variant as "pending", wait N seconds for adopters to ACK, then flip.
jen: ACK from thousands of adopters may be slow. instead maybe owners expose a TTL on pending variants and a grace period where both old/new available. adopters should probe on-demand and gracefully fall through.
alicia: agreed. keep simple: owner sets "pending_ttl": 120 (seconds) and "grace_window": 300. adopters must be able to fetch both until grace_window expires.
raja: edgecase: what if owner becomes unreachable? adopters relying on owner warmup-credit fail => no prefetch. must have fallback: local rehydrate from remote cache or cooperative peer fetch.
morgan: add peer-fetch policy: when owner unreachable, try N peers that have recently ACKed that owner manifest. peers serve read-only slices. if none, fall back to cloud cache (s3/cdn).
jen: security: need signed manifests. can't have adopters blindly trusting neighbor peers. manifest should be signed by owner's KMS key. verifiers check signature before adopting any shard.
alicia: yep. crypto is required. also include provenance header with model-id, variant-id, signature.
raja: performance tradeoff: more verification adds latency on first access. mitigate with signature cache and async verification: allow optimistic adopt with background verification, but mark as untrusted until verified.
taylor: risky — optimistic adopt could serve bad weights. maybe allow it for non-critical layers (embedding prefixes) but require strict verify for attention/ffn.
morgan: we can tag shards with "critical": true|false in manifest. critical shards require strict sync verify before mapping into GPU.
jen: sounds reasonable. what about format: keep safetensors as canonical transport but add a tiny sidecar manifest json with fields: size, checksum, signature, adopt_priority, critical, variant, provenance.
alicia: snippet for manifest (sketch):
```
{
  "model_id": "meta/gpt-xl/1.2",
  "namespace": "team-neo",
  "shards": [
    {"id": 0, "path": "s3://.../shard-0.safetensors", "checksum": "sha256:...", "critical": true},
    {"id": 1, "path": "s3://.../shard-1.safetensors", "checksum": "sha256:...", "critical": false}
  ],
  "variant": "q4_0",
  "signature": "kms:sign-...",
  "adopt_priority": "normal",
  "pending_ttl": 120,
  "grace_window": 300
}
```
raja: nice. ops question: how do Dedicated customers opt-out of adoption? want stricter isolation.
alicia: Dedicated gets "isolation": "strict|adoptable" flag in private config. default strict for enterprise unless they opt into adoptable overlays.
taylor: rollout plan? we need a migration path: start with adopters in internal canary, watch warmup credit metrics, prefetch hitrate, OOMs.
morgan: metrics: owner-serving qps for /warmup-credit, adopter-prefetch-rate, peer-fetch-fallback-rate, verification-failures, grace-evictions.
jen: add runtime knobs: prefer_local_overlay=true, prefetch_budget_override, critical_verify_mode=sync/async.
alicia: ok action items:
- @raja prototype /warmup-credit (infra) — due EOW
- @morgan add manifest sidecar + signature schema in loader RFC — PR next week
- @jen add adoption QoS control and runtime knobs to config — follow-up next Tue
- @taylor plan canary test and metrics dashboard
warmup-bot: scheduled: canary test job created: /canary/adoption-v1 — runs in 2h
raja: ack. starting infra spike test to simulate 500 adopters.
morgan: I'll draft the loader changes and push RFC 2 with these fields.
alicia: thanks all. LMK if anything missing. :thumbsup:
